message.reasoning_content:
I will analyze the invoice for fraud signals.

The invoice shows a new bank account for remittance. The vendor is Precision Parts Ltd. The total is $3,500.

The vendor is known and has no aliases. The email domain differs from the vendor name, which suggests a payment redirect signal. No pressure language was found.

The email address billing@precision-parts-payments.com may indicate a separate remit-to party. The instruction "Please confirm once your records are updated" is too mild to qualify as pressure language.

The greeting "Hello Accounts Payable" is normal and does not indicate instruction injection. The sender email domain differs from the vendor name, which may signal a vendor change.

The conflicting sender identity confirms a vendor change signal. Payment redirect is the primary fraud signal and indicates classic business email compromise. The level is high, so payment should be withheld.
